Closes #38.

pi-action no longer installs `commit-msg` or `prepare-commit-msg` hooks in the target repository. Commit conventions are the repository's job: its own hooks, CI checks, and `AGENTS.md` / `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Changes

- **`feat: stop installing git hooks in the target repository`**
  - Removes the "Install pi-agent git hooks" step from `action.yml`, and deletes `scripts/install-agent-hooks.js` and `scripts/hooks.test.js`.
  - `scripts/prepare-commit-msg.js` stays. It is this repository's own prek hook, not the injected one, so its tests move to `scripts/prepare-commit-msg.test.js`. Its knip entries and the vitest `scripts/**/*.test.js` include stay for the same reason.
  - New tests:
    - `src/entrypoints.test.ts`: `action.yml` runs only `src/index.ts` and `src/push.ts`, and its `runs:` section never mentions hooks, `core.hooksPath` or `--git-path`.
    - `src/run.test.ts`: on a checkout with `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a run where pi commits `release: v0.35.1` (the cv/pit#353 case) leaves `.git/hooks` as it was (only `*.sample`), creates no `.githooks/`, leaves the working tree clean, and keeps the commit message unchanged (no `Refs #…`).
- **`docs: say that pi follows the repository's own commit conventions`**: changes the README feature bullet and docs table, and `docs/how-it-works.md` (removes the hooks step and the "Git hooks for the agent" section, adds a "Commit conventions" section). In CONTRIBUTING it drops the links to the agent hooks and the file-table row. The current files had no README "How It Works" step 4 and no CONTRIBUTING bullet around line 167; these are the places that actually described the agent hooks.
- **`docs: add AGENTS.md that points agents to the commit conventions`**: a short root `AGENTS.md` that points to CONTRIBUTING's commit messages, `npm run check`, and the documentation style. `src/docs.test.ts` checks its links too.

`npm run check` (typecheck, lint, coverage, knip/jscpd) passes on this branch.

## ⚠️ Needs a maintainer: the commitlint CI job

The pi-action-agent App token can create PRs now, but it still can't push workflow files: `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml without workflows permission`. You can give the App the **Workflows: write** permission, or apply the commit below yourself:

```bash
gh pr checkout feat/38-no-agent-hooks
# save the patch below as ci.patch
git am ci.patch && git push
```

It adds a `commitlint` job to `ci.yml` (pull requests only) that runs `npx --no -- commitlint --from $BASE_SHA --to $HEAD_SHA --verbose` with the existing `commitlint.config.js`. It also adds the matching row in CONTRIBUTING and the line in AGENTS.md, and removes `@commitlint/cli` from knip's `ignoreDependencies`, because knip sees it used now and `--treat-config-hints-as-errors` would fail otherwise. Checked locally with the patch applied:
- `npm run check` passes.
- This PR's commits (`origin/main..HEAD`) pass commitlint with exit 0, no problems and no warnings.
- The same range plus a `release: v0.35.1` commit fails (exit 1, `type-enum`).

## Release notes (proposed for v2.3.0)

There is no CHANGELOG file; release notes live on GitHub Releases.

> ### Changed
> - **pi-action no longer installs git hooks** (#38). Before this release, the action installed a `commit-msg` hook (Conventional Commits only) and a `prepare-commit-msg` hook (`Refs #<first number in the branch name>`) in your checkout. Now pi follows your repository's own conventions: your git hooks, `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`. If you want a commit format, enforce it yourself, for example with commitlint in CI (hooks can be skipped with `--no-verify`).

## Open question: version

I went with a **minor** release (2.3.0), and the main commit is `feat:`. No inputs or outputs change. The only difference is that commits the old hook would have rejected now go through, so the changelog line above should be enough. I didn't bump `package.json`, because CONTRIBUTING has releases as their own `chore: release` commit.

## Possible follow-up (not in this PR)

pi-action doesn't put `AGENTS.md` / `CONTRIBUTING.md` into the prompt, and pi-durable doesn't load them on its own. pi only finds them when it explores the repository, and the docs are worded to match. A line in the built-in requirements block ("follow the repository's AGENTS.md / CONTRIBUTING.md when committing") would make that more reliable. That changes the prompt, so I left it out here.

open('/tmp/body.md','w').write(b)"
